newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin goes back to Kremlin to meet Russian PM.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin goes back to Kremlin to meet Russian PM.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, clearly determined to show he is fit to rule Russia, went to the Kremlin on Wednesday for the first time since he was taken ill with pneumonia two weeks ago.

The presidential press service said Yeltsin, 65, had arrived at the Kremlin at 11.30 a.m. (0830 GMT) for a meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin. It was not clear how long he would stay there.
Yeltsin moved from hospital to a country residence outside Moscow only on Monday and doctors have warned him not to rush his return to work.
His personal physician, Sergei Mironov, said on Tuesday that Yeltsin should work for just four hours a day during his convalescence.
Doctors say he is still receiving medication for double pneumonia, which affects both lungs and carries the risk of complications if it is not treated properly.
"Double pneumonia requires a rather long treatment with medicines," Mironov said. "But now on the whole the medicines are aimed at strengthening the body...It's a matter of time."
Yeltsin's return to the Kremlin coincided with a planned debate in the State Duma, the lower house of parliament, on whether to try to force the president out of office on health grounds.
Parliament's own legal department has already cast doubt on the motion, initiated by a leading opposition communist after Yeltsin was taken to hospital with pneumonia on January 8.
The legal experts have said it cannot be used to dislodge the president, who has huge powers under Russia's constitution.

Yeltsin, who had heart problems before he fell ill with pneumonia, has only spent a few days in the Kremlin since he won a second term in office on July 3. He had a heart bypass operation on November 5.
